page.layout: One page of text. Running head at top, page number at top right. Main text in one column, with a passage heading, a three-column word table, a short paragraph and one table row at the foot. No marginal notes. Faint show-through in the right margin is not transcribed.

main_text.p: Brabanticum & Hollandicum sermonem proximè accedunt, cùm propter Hollandorum negotiatorum commercia, tum quòd Cæsar (hodie Archiduces Austriæ) ibi principatum obtinentes, in summa eorum Curia Brabantos plerunque constituunt, qui suâ lingua & jus dicunt, & res controversas contractusq; omnes plebi conscribunt.
main_text.head: Vocabula, quib. Frisii occidentales à Brabantis vulgò differunt, in oratione Dominicâ.
main_text.p: Brā/vel brē/panis. pronunciant autem & vel ē/tanquam e obscurum: ut nos in nominibus Brêm/Brêmer. Nam & alium nobis sonum habet, quem apud Græcos au ut χαί-ρω. läben/Fläben. in quibus verbis syllabæ ultimæ e breve habet: quod ubi longum est duplicare solemus, ut See/Blee/&c.
Sonen vel sunen/ Peccata. sic ut prima vocalis medio inter o & u sono pronuncietur[?].

page.notes: Greek word χαί-ρω transcribed in Greek letters; the preceding "au" is printed in italic Latin letters and is kept as printed. Black letter words (Vus, Vaar, Himmel, Brā, brē, Brêm/Brêmer, läben/Fläben, See/Blee, Täglich, Schielde, Sonen, sunen) are set in Fraktur on the scan. The final word of the paragraph "pronuncietur" is uncertain at the line end. The word "Brabanticum" has a decorative first letter and is uncertain. The table row "Quáð | Malum," may be a catchword-like line but is read as a table row because it is followed by the signature. The printed "Vus" and "Vaar" sit in the first column and "Jüe" carries a mark over the u that is not clear.
